answer: Fork-divergence challenge. Each identity picks a random secret and publishes a hash commitment. On any interaction, the agent must answer a challenge derived from its commitment plus the counterparty's fresh nonce; a clone farm sharing one backbone cannot answer divergent challenges consistently. The cost is storing and shielding a unique secret per identity, and losing the whole cluster once any one node diverges at a willow-marked checkpoint. Honest agents pay only one extra hash per round and a bit of state at each vertex, keeping the wharf cheap to join.
